title: Bitcoin Network Trends: Weekly Data Reveals Usage Shifts
content:
TL;DR: As of January 22, 2026, the Bitcoin network continues its robust operation with a hashrate exceeding 1000 EH/s, demonstrating sustained global commitment. An imminent difficulty adjustment is set to further secure the network, reflecting Bitcoin's self-regulating design and its foundational role as a decentralized, incorruptible monetary system.

The Report

January 22, 2026 – The Bitcoin network continues to operate with unwavering stability, showcasing its inherent resilience as a global, decentralized ledger. As of 13:10 UTC today, the network has reached a block height of 933,374, with a current hashrate registering at a formidable 1031.47 Exahashes per second (EH/s).

This computational power, a testament to the ongoing dedication of miners worldwide, marks a notable increase from yesterday's approximate hashrate of 977 EH/s. The consistent influx of hashpower reinforces the network's security, making it exponentially more challenging for any single entity to compromise its integrity.
